purpose: Recurring MicroDuck faults: every occurrence, the hypotheses and the tests that separate them, what is only a mitigation, and whether each lost function comes back by itself. Rule: ~/code/claude-config/rules/common/recurring-fault-cause-first.md. Check: python3 microduck-sim/faults_check.py (fails while a repeated fault has no confirmed cause and no test run or queued with its blocker, or while a lost function is not shown to recover after an induced fault).

touch-twi0-jam.symptom: The head touch bus (TWI0 2510000.twi, XIAO ESP32-S3 slave 0x2A, A7Z pins 29/31) stops answering: the XIAO acks its address, every read stalls after the first data byte (kernel 'TWI BUS error state is 0x50', 'bus state 0xf9, isn't idle', 'STOP failed') and the pads stay dead until the duck is powered off.
touch-twi0-jam.required_recovery: The pads come back by themselves, with no power-off and no opening of the head. Shawn 2026-10-31: "另外你说出现问题 触摸板自己不能恢复 只能走路 这个解决方案是完全不能接受的" and "为什么你会觉得这种残疾方案可以接受呢".

hypotheses.claim: Weak pull-ups on a long bundle: only the chips' internal pull-ups (typical about 100 k on the A7Z, 45 k on the XIAO) on wires running from the head down the neck to the saddle (D-022) next to the amplifier I2S lines and, since 10/29, the microphone I2S lines (BCLK about 3 MHz while capturing). Edges too slow plus crosstalk corrupt a bit; the slave loses step.
hypotheses.for: the fault family appears 10/29, the day all three microphones were fitted and capture began; the jammed boots ran namecall's capture; 10/21 in the head with short wires: 611 reads, 0 lost
hypotheses.against: not measured: rise time and the bundle route are estimates
hypotheses.status: open

hypotheses.claim: CPU load (namecall 200-400 %) delays the TWI interrupt between bytes; a long mid-read pause trips the ESP32 slave's own timeout, which resets its state while the master continues, so the two lose step.
hypotheses.for: all recorded jams with namecall running
hypotheses.against: 2026-10-31 19:12, twi0_induce.py --pause-ms (stretch-aware bit-banged master, SCL held low mid-read, then the read finished): pauses of 5, 50, 500 and 3000 ms, 3 trials each, every block read correctly and every later kernel read fine
hypotheses.status: ruled out as a single-event trigger

hypotheses.claim: touch_main.cpp builds the reply inside onRequest with interrupts off and has no timeout or watchdog: once its TX buffer is out of step (the 10/29 filler shift) it stretches SCL on every read and never recovers.
hypotheses.for: the stall after the first data byte with the address still acked; the jam lasts until power-off; the 10/29 misalignment: reproduced 2026-10-31 19:05 by one 32-byte read of the 24-byte block (every later read starts with 0x55 and is shifted one byte; it stays shifted, RS realigns it, the brain's parser accepts the shift)
hypotheses.against: 2026-10-31 19:15 on the original firmware (1d8a9d03, same core 3.3.12): aborted reads (4), one extra SCL edge mid-read (6), a false START/STOP mid-read (6) and an over-read each left the bus answering at once; the lasting stall was not reproduced by any single event
hypotheses.status: open: persistence not reproduced by single events; T1 running

H1 predicts (b) and (d) fail; H2 predicts (c) and (d); neither: firmware only.

tests.what: induce wedges and measure the time until reads return without a power-off
tests.results: 2026-10-31 19:08-19:10, twi0_hold_test.py (XIAO holds SDA or SCL low on HD/HC, as a slave out of step does; 50 Hz reads through the bound kernel driver, nothing rebound): line watchdog paused (RD): SDA 16.9 s and 16.8 s, SCL 16.9 s stuck until the window ended; line watchdog on: SDA 5 of 5 and SCL 5 of 5 back in 0.02-0.16 s with one to seven failed reads, the kernel driver recovering by itself. mitigations: console loglevel 1 (2026-10-31 17:12): the kernel's error lines no longer starve the servo UART; 17:20 jam: brain 47 Hz, 3 of 1500 ticks missing
walk_wired.py parser length and CRC checks (bb9e9b06), touch back-off (cc0593d7), app telemetry back-off (microduck-simulator 8439ab6)

recovery.evidence: the real jam state is the XIAO holding SDA (19:19-19:27, unbound probe); the same state injected from the XIAO (HD) recovers in 0.02-0.16 s, 8 of 8 incl. 19:28 after the final flash; three real onsets on b0056 (19:46:23, 19:46:37, 19:46:43 A7Z clock: 'Arbitration lost' then 0x50 / STOP failed) each ended within 0.19 s with no power-off, and the running brain (app1031-194539, stand, new walk_wired.py) kept reading touch ('reads back' after every failure). Cold boot with the USB out: 25 of 25 reads. Recovered functions only; the onset stays open under cause.
recovery.plan: touch_main.cpp: once the bus has been idle, a line held low 30 ms restarts the whole XIAO; Wire.begin is retried every 100 ms until it succeeds; task watchdog; RS restart, RD pause and HD/HC hold commands; serial never blocks. walk_wired.py sends RS after 10 failed reads. Firmware bugs found and fixed 2026-10-31 while testing it: (1) the core's slave init refuses to start while a line is low and never retries, so a restart during a held line or during the A7Z's boot left the slave dead (069aec6a and f629c8c0 in the robot; reproduced by holding SCL 200 ms: 0 of 25 reads; fixed: 25 of 25); (2) with USB plugged in and the Mac's port closed each serial write waited 2 s and the task watchdog restarted the XIAO (fixed with setTxTimeoutMs(0), 86f9f7c7). During T1 the XIAO runs the original firmware; the new build is reflashed after it.

cause.summary: microphone capture (I2S clocks beside the touch wires, H1) makes the bit errors, confirmed by capture on/off cells 2026-10-31 20:03-20:11; a hand on the head raises the rate; the lasting jam was the XIAO slave left holding SDA, now cleared by its line watchdog
cause.fix_proposed: stiffen the lines: 2.2 kOhm pull-ups from SDA and SCL to 3V3 at the XIAO (XIAO soldering is allowed, D-013), and/or route the touch pair apart from the I2S wires in the neck; acceptance: twi0_cells_test.py capture-on cells with 0 events. Deferred by Shawn 2026-10-31 20:1x until the head is next opened ("又要开颅 肯定要以后了"); touch self-recovers meanwhile.
cause.evidence: Mechanism (19:19-19:27): a bit error on the line (first error always 'Arbitration lost') leaves the XIAO's slave a few bits out of step, driving SDA low and waiting for clocks; the sunxi driver never clocks it out, so the jam lasts until power-off. Onset: all three jammed boots had microphone capture running 2-6 min before the jam (16:30:18 -> 16:33:35, 17:11:30 -> 17:17:40, 19:17 -> 19:19:14); 16:58-17:11 without capture read fine. Shawn's hand on the head (19:28:50-19:29:27, pads 23.6k -> 30.5k, A7Z idle) gave 0 errors; mid-read pauses up to 3 s gave none (H2 ruled out). Capture alone (19:39:03-19:44:10 A7Z clock, arecord 4 ch + aplay keepalive, no brain, new firmware): 0 kernel errors in 5 min, one byte-shift at 19:42:09 (Shawn was hot-gluing the microphone backs in the head that hour). Then 19:44:22-19:47:05 another session's snap-test capture with Shawn's hands at the head (pads to 31k at 19:45:45) and, from 19:45:39, a brain in stand with torque on: 3 full onsets and 5 short ACK/STOP errors. Hand alone (no capture, no brain): 0. So no single factor triggers it here; capture with a hand at the head and/or a running brain does. Separating test queued in T1.

hypotheses.claim: The 11/04 unit has After=duck-selfcheck.service but not After=multi-user.target; duck-selfcheck is After=multi-user.target, and multi-user.target gets the implicit After=duck-namecall because it Wants it. The cycle multi-user.target -> duck-namecall -> duck-selfcheck -> multi-user.target makes systemd delete the duck-namecall start job at every boot. `systemctl restart` (the 11/04 acceptance) never builds that transaction.

hypotheses.claim: The real yaw loop (hip yaw and head yaw XL330s with backlash and deadband, low KP, the heavy head) has less damping or more delay than the sim, so stand61/walk61 feedback on a yaw disturbance is unstable on the robot and stable in sim. Predicts: sim replay of the same commands on the current model stays upright through the turn; adding yaw backlash/delay in sim reproduces the growth.
hypotheses.status: supported 2026-11-11: (a) all 14 A7Z brain logs, yaw_events.py: 24 full-window turn stops, 6 grew (4 fell), 25 %; even the 18 that settled peaked at 1-3 rad/s yaw in the first second; (b) current-model sim of the same turn stop (vtheta -0.3 for 1.5 s): nominal delay peaks 0.9-1.1 rad/s and decays to 0.02 within 1 s; +20 ms action delay (--action-delay 2) peaks 3.6 and keeps 2.5 rad/s in s 1-3 (seed 1), tilt 7-17 deg across seeds; +40 ms falls even standing still; (c) the robot's transport latency is short (joint sample to goal write 16 ms median, IMU 21 ms), shorter than the sim default (about 44 ms). So the real robot carries roughly 40 ms more effective lag than the sim, in the servo and body response, not in the bus. Training saw action delay 15-30 ms, KP exactly 200 (KP DR off) and friction 0.9-1.1x.

hypotheses.claim: The head_pose command (head yaw -0.355 with neck 0.35) or the post-turn state lies outside the policy's training distribution. Predicts: the same disturbance inside the trained range does not grow.
hypotheses.status: weakened 2026-11-11: -0.355 rad is inside the trained head-yaw range (+-1.40); 76 of 77 full-window head-yaw steps in all logs settled

hypotheses.claim: A hand or the cable touched the robot (run 2 leg current jumped 271 -> 816 mA in one tick at +339.09 before the gyro grew).
hypotheses.status: open for 11-11 run 2 only (the one head step of 77 that grew); no video

hypotheses.claim: Pollen's robotd low-pass filters the policy targets (legs alpha 0.7, head 0.5) and scales walking actions by 0.9 and by 7.4 V / battery; robotd.toml says the alpha policies (walk61, stand61) were trained with that filter. walk_wired sends targets unfiltered and unscaled (a uniform 0.5 goal EMA trial on 2026-10-16 was inconclusive and removed). Run 2's growing head-yaw action is what an unfiltered head target with too much loop gain looks like. Predicts: sim replay with the robotd filter damps the growth where the unfiltered replay does not; on the robot the head-yaw step (T3) settles with the filter.
hypotheses.status: rejected 2026-11-11 (Shawn: "加滤波肯定不是一个好的方式 我们之前试过很多次"): no evidence separates it from H1. Against it: the 2026-10-16 robot trial (goal EMA 0.5) left the action jumps unchanged and fell once at the stop in three walks (walk_wired.py:1249); the 2026-10-29 sim check of robotd's 0.7/0.5 low-pass on the rise still fell 2 of 4; the public microduck_rl trains walk61's family unfiltered (low-pass reverted 2026-07-07); a low-pass adds phase lag, which feeds a growing oscillation rather than damping it. Not to be tried again without a new discriminating result.

tests.results: delay grid (out/yawgrid on the Mac mini mirror ~/sims/fullflow-20261111): action delay 1-2 ticks stands in head and turn cases, 3+ ticks falls even before the disturbance; BAM friction 1.5x raises the turn's peak tilt from 3-4 to 8-11 deg; +20 ms reproduces the real post-stop yaw amplitude. Backlash not yet tried. KP grid 2026-11-11 (out/kpgrid, out/kpgrid2, out/walkgrid): under 2-tick delay KP 250/300 are worse (all turn stops fall at 250); KP 160/180 settle the -0.3 and -0.5 turn stops (post-stop yaw 0.01-0.11 rad/s vs KP 200 up to 3.3). But no single sim setting matches the robot: with 2-tick delay KP 200 also falls mid-walk at vx 0.25 (3 of 3), while the robot walks steadily at KP 200; with 1-tick delay turn stops never grow. Lower KP also costs: at 1.5x friction KP 160 falls right after a walk stops (3 of 3, 1-tick delay) where KP 200 does not. So the delay knob alone does not reproduce the robot, and a runtime KP change is not supported by the sim as a fix; it can only be judged on the robot.

hypotheses.claim: The lean is not built into one joint. After a walk the policy at zero command holds the robot at KP 200, where loaded joints sit 2 to 6 deg short of their goals; the left leg ends the walk carrying more, sags more, the body tips further left and the left leg carries more still. Stand mode at KP 400 pulls the legs back to a mirrored pose and the lean drops to about 1 deg.
hypotheses.status: open; supported by the 2026-11-12 20:10 log (same robot, same minute: 1.1 deg at KP 400, 2.3 deg at KP 200 after the walk). Not yet separated from H3 for the remaining 1 deg

hypotheses.claim: The roll sits at the left foot: either the hand-applied sole (hot glue coat of 2026-10-21 plus the black pad) is thicker under the inner edge, or the left foot sits tilted on its two-half ankle bracket.
hypotheses.status: withdrawn 2026-11-12: Shawn sees no thickness difference in the sole layer ("鞋底也没有肉眼可见的厚薄区别"), and the encoders already explain the sole angle (H7)

hypotheses.claim: There is no ankle roll joint, so a sole's side tilt is pelvis roll plus hip roll minus about 3.7 deg (the hip roll at which the sole lies flat; from target_ground at the logged poses, both legs). Walk mode at zero command holds the left hip roll at 6.6 to 6.9 deg and the right at 5.3 to 6.7: both soles sit on their outer edges (left 3 deg, right 1.6 to 3), a V that cannot rest level, so the robot tips to the wider side, the left; the 2.3 to 2.6 deg lean then adds to the left sole (5 to 6 deg) and flattens the right. Stand mode holds 4.5 / 4.5 (0.8 deg each) and leans 1.1 to 1.8.
hypotheses.status: supported: predicted and scanned sole angles agree in both 11-12 scans; the sim policy at zero command holds 4.7 / 4.3 and stands at roll 0.2 (lean-t3 base). Open: why the robot's policy holds the hips 1 to 2.5 deg wider than the sim's (its hip roll actions are R -0.079 L -0.030 against the sim's -0.057 / -0.003)

tests.what: brain_sim_check.py: walk 4 s then zero command 30 s, with and without a 1 deg starting asymmetry; does the sim policy at KP 200 settle into the same uneven stance (hip pitch 4.5 deg apart, roll over 2 deg)?
tests.results: 2026-11-12, Mac mini ~/sims/lean-t3 (asbuilt current, --volt 7.6 --drop 0.036 --imu-pitch 2, walk 3.6 s at 0.25, --after-walk 30). Roll before the walk / 5-15 s after / last 10 s: no offset 0.00 / 0.15 / 0.26; mass 3 mm left 0.29 / 0.63 / 0.69; mass 6 mm left 0.52 / 1.30 / 1.21 (robot 1.1 / 2.3 / 2.35). In every case the sim also ends with the left hip pitch 2 to 3 deg less bent than the right and the left ankle 2 to 3 deg less (robot 4.5 and 2.9): the uneven fore-aft stance after a walk is the policy's own and not a robot defect. The sim roughly doubles a sideways offset after the walk, as the robot does (H5 supported). What the sim does not show: its left hip roll moves inward as it tips left (R 5.6 / L 3.5), the robot's moves outward (R 5.3 / L 6.6); and the robot needs more than the 6 mm offset to start at 1.1 deg

tests.what: Find what makes walk61 at zero command hold the hips wider on the robot than in the sim: replay the robot's logged observations (app1112-2010, 20:04-20:06) through walk61 and compare its hip roll actions with the sim's at the same pose; then test in the sim the inputs that differ (roll reading, hip roll tracking error at KP 200)
tests.results: 2026-11-12 (play-locate-20261112/t7_replay.py, t7_course.py, t7_run_batch.sh; Mac mini ~/sims/lean-t7, 36 sims). WORDING FIX: 'wider hips' in this fault means a larger hip roll magnitude, and in the model that is the leg turned INWARD (left_hip_roll + = counter-clockwise from the front = left foot outward; the robot's left reads -6.6 to -6.9; +3 deg moves the left foot 4 mm outward, ~/sims/stance.py). ACTION ORDER FIX: action follows OBSERVATION_DOF_ORDER, not servo ID order; the 'R -0.079 / L -0.030' quoted in T3 were left knee and head roll. Measured, robot 20:04:10-20:05:40: default 4.98 / 4.98, goal R 8.62 / L 7.82, position 5.32 / 6.59. Sim lean-t3 base: goal 10.55 / 10.86, position 4.80 / 4.36. So the policy asks for MORE hip roll in the sim than on the robot, and neither reaches its goal: with both feet on the ground the hip roll is set by where the feet stand, not by the goal (--kp-rl 300 moves the goals, not the positions). Offline replay reproduces the logged actions within 0.0002 rad; swapping input groups shows the action difference comes from the joint position feedback (a larger hip roll reading makes the policy ask for less), gravity only about 1 deg on the left. Time course: the robot reaches hip roll sum 11.9 within 1.5 s of zero command and does not move for 100 s; the sim stops at 11.7 and creeps back to 9.05 in 20 s. No sim flag reproduces the robot (closest: --joint-play 6 on left_hip_roll only, 5.58 / 5.48, roll 1.6). Inference, not verified: the robot's feet stay where the last steps put them (floor friction, gear stiction) and the sim's creep back. Every standstill in the log (scratchpad t7_stops.py): stand KP 400 4.4 / 4.4 roll +1.8 and +1.2; walk mode 5.3 / 6.6 roll +2.3 (twice), 4.0 / 4.9 roll +2.1 (4 s), 6.7 / 6.9 roll +2.6: the lean is 1.2 to 1.8 deg even with level hips, so the hip roll explains the sole angle but not all of the pelvis roll.
